explain.say: Long before writing, the griots of West Africa kept history alive by voice. For centuries they have sung the epic of Sunjata, founder of the Mali Empire, passing it from parent to child. Oral history is the modern method of recording people's spoken memories. The chain on the board shows how a historian does it.

explain.say: Oral history is worldwide. Look at the map. In the 1930s the United States Federal Writers' Project recorded more than 2,300 formerly enslaved people. In recent years the 1947 Partition Archive has recorded thousands of survivors of the partition of India and Pakistan. Why might these voices be missing from official papers?

Now look at the second link: consent. You are borrowing someone's life story, so the narrator must agree how it will be recorded, kept and used. Many remember painful events, so a good interviewer listens patiently and never pushes. Why does trust change what people tell you?

draw.text: British pioneer: Paul Thompson, The Voice of the Past (1978).

explain.say: Is memory reliable? See the two columns. The Italian historian Alessandro Portelli found that workers in Terni remembered a comrade's 1949 death as happening during 1953 strikes. The date was wrong, but the mistake showed what the death meant to them. So errors can be evidence. What would you check it against?

The best oral historians combine voices with documents, letting each test the other. You did really well. Here is your challenge: interview an older relative about one day they remember clearly, then find one document, photo or newspaper that confirms or questions their story.

faq.a: Oral history is the recording and study of people's spoken memories of the past, usually through recorded interviews. It also includes long oral traditions such as the griots' epics in West Africa.

Memory can shift with time, later events and the interview itself, so oral history must be checked against other sources. But it gives evidence of experience and meaning that documents often miss, and even its errors can be revealing.
asks: Can we trust memories as evidence?

faq.a: Portelli found that people in Terni, Italy, remembered the 1949 killing of the worker Luigi Trastulli as part of 1953 strikes. He argued the shifted date showed how the community understood the event, so memory's errors carry meaning.
asks: What is the Luigi Trastulli story?

faq.q: Why does consent matter in oral history?
faq.a: Because a narrator shares their own life. Ethical practice means explaining the project, getting agreement on recording, archiving and publication, and respecting requests to keep parts private.
asks: What are the ethics of oral history?

faq.q: What were the WPA slave narratives?
faq.a: Between 1936 and 1938 the Federal Writers' Project of the Works Progress Administration interviewed more than 2,300 formerly enslaved people in the United States. The records are invaluable but were shaped by mostly white interviewers in the segregated South.
asks: What is the Federal Writers' Project slave narrative collection?

facts: The Federal Writers' Project recorded more than 2,300 first-person accounts of slavery between 1936 and 1938.
Paul Thompson's The Voice of the Past was first published in 1978.
The Sunjata epic about the founder of the Mali Empire has been passed down by griots for centuries.

quiz.say: What did Portelli's Terni interviews show?

options.show: Wrong dates in memories can reveal meaning
options.say: Wrong dates in memories can reveal meaning

quiz.why: The misremembered date showed how people linked the death to later struggles, so memory's shape was itself evidence.

wrong.1: Portelli argued the opposite: oral sources are valuable when read carefully.
wrong.2: The point was that memory differed from the records.

quiz.say: Which step comes before recording an oral history interview?
quiz.show: What must come before you record?
quiz.why: Consent comes first: the narrator agrees how the interview will be recorded, kept and used.

wrong.0: Publishing comes last, and only as agreed.
wrong.2: Archiving happens after recording and transcription.
